correctness.rationale: The second-order ratio hypothesis yields a_n=c(n+1)^(-s)(1+O(1/n)), so R_a is Hilbert-Schmidt. Its exact K_ij entry formula has eventually negative coordinate diagonal with coefficient -2(s-1)c^2/(2s-1) and normalized off-diagonal decays as j^(-1/2), giving negative subspaces of arbitrarily large finite dimension. For v_j=e_j-2e_(j+1)+e_(j+2), exact adjoint computations give q_j=2s a_j^2/(j+1)(1+O(1/j)) positive with normalized off-diagonal O(j^(-3/2)), giving positive subspaces of every dimension. Strict diagonal dominance and compact self-adjoint spectral theory complete the proof; 182 supplemental assertions passed, not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Known nonhyponormality of compact Rhaly matrices asserts only at least one negative direction, and neither trace zero nor ideal membership implies infinite two-sided inertia. The new theorem completely determines the qualitative infinite signed multiplicities for all positive smoothly power-decaying Rhaly rows, including all shifted powers, thus resolving a natural structural defect question and exhibiting a sharp qualitative contrast with the subnormal Cesàro endpoint.
